clue.text: Facial hair (and fringe) goes up in smoke

blocks.note: a fringe is an edge or side of something
something that goes up in smoke burns

explanation.surface: Someone's whiskers and fringe catch fire and go up in smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket makes 'and fringe' look like part of the hairstyle, but 'and' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideburns are strips of hair grown down the sides of a man's face in front of the ears.

clue.text: Spell isn't broken on time

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

blocks.note: the word as written, apostrophe dropped
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A magic spell that refuses to break down when the clock demands it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' suggests magic, but here it is a period of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A stint and a spell are both synonyms for a period of time spent doing a job or duty.

clue.text: Animal missing? Blast it!

blocks.note: a dog is an animal
something missing has gone

explanation.surface: Someone discovers their pet has vanished and swears in frustration.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggone is a mild American curse word, used like darn or damn as an exclamation of annoyance.

clue.text: Woman embraced by doctor making proclamation

indicators.note: being embraced by means being held inside another's arms, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: BS is Bachelor of Surgery, a medical degree
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman hugged by her doctor as some announcement is made.
explanation.walkthrough: Banns are the public announcement in church of a planned marriage, read so objections can be raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Banns are a formal public announcement of an intended wedding, read out in a parish church.

clue.text: Character told to clean fish fillet

indicators.note: told means spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the one meaning character

blocks.note: a character in a play is a role
to mop is to clean a floor

explanation.surface: An actor is instructed to scrub a piece of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first part is a sound-alike: role, heard as ROLL; MOP is taken straight.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a pickled herring fillet rolled up, often around onion or gherkin.

clue.text: Small burial chamber containing writing material, book and source of foul smell

indicators.note: a thing containing others holds them inside, so the chamber wraps around what follows

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a tomb is a burial chamber
ink is what you write with
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A list of things found in a small tomb, ending with something that reeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' applies to the burial chamber only: the small S stays outside, in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A stink bomb is a small prank device that releases a horrible odour when broken.

clue.text: Man taking drugs from Native American

indicators.note: taking something from a word removes it, leaving the rest behind

blocks.note: the Pawnee are a Native American people of the Great Plains
E is ecstasy, so two Es are drugs

explanation.surface: A man getting narcotics from a Native American dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece here, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess every piece is called a man, and the pawn is the humblest of those pieces.

clue.text: Fathers holding short bear close to little baby carrier

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter of the following name is lost
holding means gripping inside, so the fathers wrap around what follows
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father, plural PAS
Pooh is the famous bear of A. A. Milne's stories
the final letter of little

explanation.surface: Dads cuddling a teddy bear near their little one.
explanation.walkthrough: The bear is Winnie-the-Pooh; 'short' docks his final letter before he goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A papoose is a bag or pouch for carrying an infant on the back, originally a Native American word for a baby.

clue.text: See 14
Pure river spirit found in small container

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so these pieces sit within the container named next

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
gin is a spirit
a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: Clean water and liquor discovered inside a little bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests a ghost, but here it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginal means chaste or untouched, in a state of purity like a virgin.

clue.text: Slim pedestrian carrying hamper

indicators.note: the words before it are carrying the answer inside them, spanning the two words

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A thin walker lugging a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like a basket, but it is the verb meaning hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper someone is to hinder or obstruct their progress, which is what impede means.

clue.text: Waste product generated by special agents

blocks.note: first meaning: bodily waste, faeces
second meaning: police informers, short for stool pigeons

explanation.surface: Pollution produced by a team of secret operatives.
explanation.walkthrough: A stool, or stool pigeon, is slang for an informer planted to spy for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a medical term for excrement and also slang for informers who work secretly for police.

clue.text: Force completed reorganisation

blocks.note: to make someone do something is to force them
something completed is over

explanation.surface: A police force has finished its restructuring.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeover is a thorough transformation or renovation of something's appearance or structure.

clue.text: Leaves theses unbound

indicators.note: unbound means untied and loose, so the letters are free to move around

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Pages of dissertations that have come away from their binding.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves of paper are single pages, which is also what sheets of paper are.

clue.text: That man with nuclear particles is extremely difficult

indicators.note: particles are fragments, so the word before is broken up into its letters and rebuilt

blocks.note: he refers to that man
the letters to rearrange; with just joins

explanation.surface: A physicist working with atomic particles is finding the job very hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculean tasks are those so demanding they would need the strength of Hercules, the mythical hero of twelve labours.

clue.text: Swedish fly deafened unbalanced English football team

indicators.note: unbalanced means unsteady or deranged, so the letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: all three words supply the letters

explanation.surface: An insect from Sweden, its ears ruined, now flies erratically.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheffield Wednesday are a football club from the northern English city of Sheffield.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheffield Wednesday is a long-established professional English football club based in South Yorkshire.

clue.text: Money made by professional joining top players in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: pro is short for professional
seeds are top-ranked players in a tennis tournament

explanation.surface: An actor's earnings after joining star performers at a tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' suggests theatre, but here it simply means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Proceeds are the sum of money earned from a sale or event.

clue.text: Employer wearing retro type of pants?

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the following word is read from its end
something being worn is put inside clothing, so the first piece goes inside

blocks.note: a type is a sort
someone who employs a tool is a user

explanation.surface: A boss dressed in an old-fashioned style of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that pants means trousers in American English; in Britain pants are underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage pants are trousers, the leg-covering garment, so the definition fits by a transatlantic sense.

clue.text: Daft tip-off given to newspaper covering earl's offence

indicators.note: with its tip off, the word before loses its first letter

blocks.note: daft means dumb, stupid
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A foolish tip passed to a paper, reporting an aristocrat's misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'covering' puts RAG above E.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, so umbrage means a feeling of resentment or annoyance.

clue.text: Grains sprinkled on American drink

indicators.note: sprinkled things are scattered about, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Seeds scattered over an American cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine, fruit and sometimes brandy.

clue.text: See 26
Division of leaf on large heart of speciality plant

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so just the middle letters of the next word are kept

blocks.note: a lobe is a rounded section of a leaf
L is the abbreviation for large
the two central letters of speciality

explanation.surface: A botanist's note about the large section of a leaf in their area of expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a flowering garden plant, often grown for its small blue blooms in borders.

clue.text: Old note found in burnt out part of engine

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters before it are rearranged
found in means sitting inside, so these pieces go within the jumbled word

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
O is the abbreviation for old
fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An old memo discovered in a burnt-out section of an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbofan is a jet engine type, and also the large fan stage at its front driven by the turbine.

clue.text: Dishes in Bake Off served with hollowed biscuits

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters before it are rearranged
hollowed means emptied out, so only the outside letters of the next word remain

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
first and last letters of biscuits

explanation.surface: Meals on a TV baking show presented alongside biscuits with their middles scooped out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great British Bake Off is a popular British TV baking competition; its title supplies the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Kebabs are dishes of grilled meat and vegetables, often served on skewers.

clue.text: Son abandoning rough drawing of sailing boat

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a sketch is a rough drawing

explanation.surface: A boy leaves behind his doodle of a yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel with the mizzen mast set forward of the rudder.

clue.text: Doctor shed tears over breast

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the joined pieces read from bottom to top

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: A physician weeps over a patient's chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosom is a word for a person's chest, especially a woman's breasts.

clue.text: Clubber at event holding dress down

indicators.note: the words before it are holding the answer within them, across their boundaries

blocks.note: found running across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A nightclubber at a party is wearing casual clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress down' looks like wearing casual clothes, but it is the idiom for a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a dressing-down is to scold them severely, which is to berate them.

clue.text: Harsh regulations restricting time at hospital allotted to head of surgery

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the rules enclose what follows
the head is the top, so only the first letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: regulations are rules
T is the abbreviation for time
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
first letter of surgery

explanation.surface: Strict rules limiting hospital time given to the chief surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: T and H, joined by 'at', sit inside RULES; then S is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless means without pity or mercy, so harsh and cruel in treatment of others.

clue.text: Foreign nanny nursing European throwback to English queen

indicators.note: foreign means strange and unfamiliar, so the word after it is rearranged
nursing means cradling something in one's arms, so the scrambled letters hold the rest

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
E is the abbreviation for European
a throw is a lob, and back turns it round
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An overseas nanny cares for a European child who resembles an English queen of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwback' looks like one word for an ancestral likeness, but it splits into a throw and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Boleyn was the second wife of Henry VIII and Queen of England until her execution in 1536.

clue.text: Doctored graph stopping virgin on the rebound getting contraceptive

indicators.note: doctored means tampered with, so the letters of the next word are rearranged
on the rebound means bouncing back, so the word is read from its end
stopping means plugging a gap, so the jumbled piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
a maid is an old word for a virgin

explanation.surface: A falsified chart stops a young woman, newly out of a relationship, from obtaining birth control.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaphragm is a dome-shaped cap worn inside the body as a barrier form of birth control.
